items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1959-07-16
items.q: Tony Fugierat's the, the cornet player.

ctx.x: Well, they didn't live across the river then. No. Well, I thought maybe they were from over there. They never did live across, no, the Hardys lived across the river, you see.

I mean, they Hardys probably all did. And, and, and, and Emmett's sister and the Boswell kids were, were, were real friendly. And that's how, how, how Emmett happened to go to the Boswell's house, through his sister. And they had a, they had a, a little trio. They played, they played both. When they played classical, Connie would play the cello, Martha would play the piano, and Vett would play the violin. And when they played jazz, Vett would play the banjo, Connie, uh, Martha would play the piano. And, uh, and,…

items.title: Tony Fougerat Interview, 1960-06-08
items.q: And I think Monk Hazel played in that band too with him.

ctx.x: Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm.

Mm-hm. well they called them cafes in them days, on Rampart Street. Him and King Oliver was playing together. Loey was playing the second trumpet. I never will forget that. And I was just starting out and I heard so much about Loey. And I went in there and heard him playing. And then in later years after he got playing good there, there was a little boy come up there by the name of Emmett Harding. He was very good. And Emmett was playing with a band by the name of Brownlee, who was a bass player. And Brownlee was…
You talked about Rene, and you were saying how good he was.
